blocks.raw: # Configuring earning and allocation rules
blocks.text: Configuring earning and allocation rules

blocks.raw: By default, a transaction issues points both to the member's individual wallet and their associated group's wallet. To direct points to just the group wallet instead, configure a mutually exclusive workflow in Loyalty+. This ensures a single transaction credits either the group wallet or the personal wallet, but not both.

blocks.raw: ## Prerequisites
blocks.text: Prerequisites

blocks.raw: Before you begin, confirm the following prerequisites are in place:
blocks.text: Before you begin, confirm the following prerequisites are in place:

blocks.raw:
* User group loyalty is enabled for your organization.
* A transaction-level extended field exists (for example, `member_card_swiped`) with values `Yes` and `No`.
* Your POS or API integration passes this extended field in the `AddTransaction` payload: `Yes` for a group transaction, `No` or null for a standard individual transaction.

blocks.raw: To configure the workflow:

1. Go to **Loyalty+ > Programs** and select your program.
2. Select **Edit Program**, then open the **Workflows** tab.
3. Create a new workflow condition triggered by the **TransactionAdd** customer activity, or edit an existing one.
4. In the **Expressions** box, add the following condition for individual transactions:
blocks.text: Go to Loyalty+ > Programs and select your program.Select Edit Program, then open the Workflows tab.Create a new workflow condition triggered by the TransactionAdd customer activity, or edit an existing one.In the Expressions box, add the following condition for individual transactions:

```
currentTxn.extField_membership_card_swiped=="No" || currentTxn.extField_membership_card_swiped.isNull( )
```
In the above expression example, `membership_card_swiped` is the extended field enabled for identifying user group related transactions.

blocks.raw: # Configuring currency expiry
blocks.text: Configuring currency expiry

blocks.raw: Point expiry for group wallets can follow the same rules as individual expiry or use a separate configuration, depending on your program's needs. Both approaches are configured under the action in the **Workflows** section.
blocks.text: Point expiry for group wallets can follow the same rules as individual expiry or use a separate configuration, depending on your program's needs. Both approaches are configured under the action in the Workflows section.

blocks.raw: For fleet programs, enabling `FLEET_GROUP_LOYALTY_ENABLED` and setting the `FLEET_ENTITY_TYPE` parameter activates expiry logic for fleet group users. This applies to all group loyalty programs using the fleet construct.
blocks.text: For fleet programs, enabling FLEET_GROUP_LOYALTY_ENABLED and setting the FLEET_ENTITY_TYPE parameter activates expiry logic for fleet group users. This applies to all group loyalty programs using the fleet construct.

blocks.raw: For details on configuring expiry conditions in workflows, refer to the [Expiry Conditions](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/points#expiry-conditions) documentation.
blocks.text: For details on configuring expiry conditions in workflows, refer to the Expiry Conditions documentation.

blocks.raw: # Configuring redemption rules
blocks.text: Configuring redemption rules

blocks.raw: To enable point redemption at the group level in a Multi-Loyalty Program (MLP) environment, the `ENABLE_GROUP_PROGRAMS_REDEMPTION` flag must be active for your organisation. Without this flag, redemption API calls at the group level will fail regardless of member permissions. To enable this, raise a JIRA ticket to the Capillary product support team.
blocks.text: To enable point redemption at the group level in a Multi-Loyalty Program (MLP) environment, the ENABLE_GROUP_PROGRAMS_REDEMPTION flag must be active for your organisation. Without this flag, redemption API calls at the group level will fail regardless of member permissions. To enable this, raise a JIRA ticket to the Capillary product support team.

blocks.raw: If your organisation uses a single loyalty program (not MLP), this flag is not be required.
blocks.text: If your organisation uses a single loyalty program (not MLP), this flag is not be required.

blocks.raw: Redemption permissions are controlled at the member level:
blocks.text: Redemption permissions are controlled at the member level:

blocks.raw:
* Primary members can always redeem from the shared wallet.
* Secondary members can redeem only if the `allow_points_redemption` [permission](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/creating-and-managing-groups#assigning-permissions-to-a-member) is granted at join time.
* To restrict a member from redeeming, pass `block_points_redemption` in as the [permission](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/creating-and-managing-groups#assigning-permissions-to-a-member)  when adding them to the group.
blocks.text: Primary members can always redeem from the shared wallet.Secondary members can redeem only if the allow_points_redemption permission is granted at join time.To restrict a member from redeeming, pass block_points_redemption in as the permission  when adding them to the group.

blocks.raw: # Tracking points per program
blocks.text: Tracking points per program

blocks.raw: In a Multi-Loyalty Program (MLP) environment, you can configure the system to calculate and track group points separately per program rather than as a single combined total. When enabled, each program maintains its own independent points balance for the group.
blocks.text: In a Multi-Loyalty Program (MLP) environment, you can configure the system to calculate and track group points separately per program rather than as a single combined total. When enabled, each program maintains its own independent points balance for the group.

blocks.raw: **Example:** A group has members enrolled in Program A and Program B. Points earned via Program A transactions are tracked in the Program A group wallet, and points from Program B go into the Program B wallet. Redemptions draw from the respective program wallet, not a combined pool.
blocks.text: Example: A group has members enrolled in Program A and Program B. Points earned via Program A transactions are tracked in the Program A group wallet, and points from Program B go into the Program B wallet. Redemptions draw from the respective program wallet, not a combined pool.

blocks.raw: Enable the `CONF_ENABLE_GROUP_POINTS_BY_PROGRAM` flag by raising a JIRA ticket to the Capillary product support team.
blocks.text: Enable the CONF_ENABLE_GROUP_POINTS_BY_PROGRAM flag by raising a JIRA ticket to the Capillary product support team.

blocks.raw: # Transferring points
blocks.text: Transferring points

blocks.raw: Points can be transferred between individual accounts and group wallets using the [Transfer Group Points API](https://docs.capillarytech.com/reference/transfer-group-points) (`POST /v2/points/userGroup2/transfer`). The following transfer directions are supported:
blocks.text: Points can be transferred between individual accounts and group wallets using the Transfer Group Points API (POST /v2/points/userGroup2/transfer). The following transfer directions are supported:

blocks.raw:
* Individual to Group
* Group to Individual
* Group to Group
blocks.text: Individual to GroupGroup to IndividualGroup to Group

blocks.raw: To target a group wallet as the destination, set `"type": "USERGROUP2"` in the `toEntity` object. Without this, the transfer defaults to an individual account.
blocks.text: To target a group wallet as the destination, set "type": "USERGROUP2" in the toEntity object. Without this, the transfer defaults to an individual account.
